# [TASK] Frontend: RTK Query endpoint for POST /api/v1/ai/recommendations

## Task
Add the RTK Query endpoint and FE service call to `POST /api/v1/ai/recommendations`.

## Scope
Data-fetching layer only — the view rendering the results is a separate Task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] RTK Query endpoint added, follows the existing pattern in `services/AI.js` (`aiApi.getMovieRecommendations`, `useGetMovieRecommendationsQuery`) (`AI.test.js`, `aiApi.getMovieRecommendations (#220)`)
- [x] Request body built from Task #219's identified `recentMovies` source (Favorites, titles resolved via TMDB), plus a requested `count` (`AI.test.js: "resolves favorites to titles via TMDB and posts them as recentMovies, plus count"`)
- [x] Loading, empty (no history), and error states are distinct and observable from the hook's return value — `isLoading`/`isFetching` from RTK Query itself, `data.isEmpty` for no favorites, `error` for a real failure, including the case where every favorite's TMDB lookup fails rather than none existing (`AI.test.js`, the isEmpty/error/`"errors instead of calling /recommendations when every TMDB lookup fails"` tests)
- [x] Uses the dynamic base query / `resolveApiUrl` pattern already used elsewhere, not a hardcoded URL (`AI.test.js: "resolves favorites..." asserts the full request URL`)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 4

## Notes
Implemented as a custom `queryFn` (not a plain `query`) because building the request means dispatching two other APIs' endpoints first: `userApi.getFavorites` for ids, then one `tmdbApi.getMovie` per id for titles. `keepUnusedDataFor: 0`, since the backend refreshes the user's taste profile as a side effect of every call, so the result must not be served from a stale cache.

A total TMDB-resolution failure (favorites exist, but every title lookup fails) is reported as an error rather than an empty, successful, unpersonalized response, since the two would otherwise look identical. `keepUnusedDataFor: 0` prevents a stale-cache read from this side-effecting call, but does not refetch when a favorite is added or removed while the view stays mounted; #221 calls `refetch()` after such a change if that proves necessary.
